statement: Let G be a planar graph, v a vertex of degree 5, and c a proper 4-coloring of G-v in which all four colors appear on the neighbors of v; then some single Kempe-chain interchange (swapping two colors on one connected component of the subgraph induced by those two color classes) leaves at most three colors on the neighbors of v, so c extends to a 4-coloring of G.
definitions: Planar graph = finite simple graph drawable in the plane without crossings. Proper coloring = adjacent vertices receive distinct colors. For two colors a,b a Kempe chain is a connected component of the subgraph of G-v induced by the vertices colored a or b; a single Kempe-chain interchange swaps a and b on exactly one such component and changes nothing else. 'Leaves at most three colors on the neighbors of v' refers to the coloring after the interchange; c 'extends' means v can then be given a fourth color.
ground_truth_witness: The Errera graph, a planar triangulation on vertices 0..16 with the 45 edges 0-1 0-7 0-14 0-15 0-16 1-2 1-9 1-14 1-15 2-3 2-8 2-9 2-10 2-14 3-4 3-9 3-10 3-11 4-5 4-10 4-11 4-12 5-6 5-11 5-12 5-13 6-7 6-8 6-12 6-13 6-16 7-13 7-15 7-16 8-10 8-12 8-14 8-16 9-11 9-13 9-15 10-12 11-13 13-15 14-16. Take v = 0, whose 5 neighbors are 1, 7, 14, 15, 16. The following proper 4-coloring c of G-0 (colors 0..3) uses all four colors on N(0): 1:0, 2:1, 3:0, 4:1, 5:0, 6:2, 7:3, 8:0, 9:3, 10:2, 11:2, 12:3, 13:1, 14:3, 15:2, 16:1. Here c(1)=0, c(7)=3, c(14)=3, c(15)=2, c(16)=1. There are exactly 10 Kempe chains (over all 6 color pairs and all components), and interchanging any one of them leaves all four colors on N(0), so no single interchange frees a color for vertex 0. This is the gap in Kempe's 1879 'proof' of the four color theorem.

skeptic.objection: Precise universal claim over (G, v, c). Reference verified by computation: 17 vertices, 45 = 3n-6 edges, every vertex link is a single cycle, 30 triangular faces, V-E+F = 2 (and networkx check_planarity confirms; 5-connected); the given c is a proper 4-coloring of G-0, N(0) = {1,7,14,15,16} carries all four colors, there are exactly 10 Kempe chains over the 6 color pairs, and no single interchange reduces the number of colors on N(0). G is 4-colorable (so a solver cannot refute via non-colorability; the refutation must attack the 'single interchange suffices' step). Genuine construction: solver must exhibit a planar graph + coloring where every single swap fails (Errera/Kittell/Heawood, or 9-vertex Soifer/Fritsch examples) and check all chains. No roster or surplus item concerns Kempe chains.

bank_overlap.rationale: grep errera returns nothing. se-math-3224334-q is about Kempe's degree-5 case but refutes a different step (two simultaneous Kempe swaps justified from the original coloring can be improper) with a 7-vertex witness in which a single 1-3 swap at x1 already reduces N(v) to three colors, so it does not refute the task's single-interchange claim and is not the Errera graph.
